answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers one trellis row. A public sun-map lists each row's shade footprint for audit. A new row in the garden compensates every row it shades, so the kth row pays 12(k-1): the 1000th pays 11,988, and 1,000 fakes pay 5,994,000 plus 70,000 locked. Each payment sends a ripple across neighboring rows, so underpayment shows on the ledger. A rented-shade ring stacking rows to hide footprints fails when the sun-map exposes the overlap and burns every stacked bond. One honest grower pays 70 plus 12 once, recovering the bond after a clean audit.
